wizard.welcomeBody: Your entire game and software library, beautifully organized. Let's find everything installed on your PC.
wizard.drivesBody: Playnest always checks your Start Menu & installed apps list. Pick drives for a deeper scan.
wizard.deepScanDesc: Also searches Program Files & Games folders for apps not in your Start Menu. Slower, more thorough.
wizard.scanningBody: This usually takes under a minute.
wizard.doneBody: Playnest found {count} games and applications on your PC.
wizard.doneTip: Tip: you can re-run this scan anytime from Settings to pick up newly installed games.
wizard.skipConfirmBody: You can scan your PC anytime later from Settings. Your library will be empty until then.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Changes apply immediately across the whole app.
settings.apiKeyHint: Cover art needs a free SteamGridDB key — grab one from your SteamGridDB account, then paste it here.
settings.coverArtHint: Fetch artwork for any games or apps that don't have it yet — no need to re-run the whole scan.
settings.libraryHealthHint: Check that every entry in your library still exists on disk — catches games you've since uninstalled or moved, or drives that are no longer connected.
settings.backupHint: Save your whole library — including favorites, collections, and playtime — to a file you control, or restore from one.
settings.libraryHint: Re-scan your PC to pick up newly installed games and apps.
settings.trayTitle: Keep Playnest running in the tray
settings.trayDesc: Closing the window minimizes to the tray instead of quitting, so your favorites are always one click away. Quit from the tray icon to fully close.
settings.quickLaunchTitle: Enable Ctrl+Shift+L to jump to Playnest
settings.quickLaunchDesc: Works even when Playnest isn't focused — brings the window to the front and jumps straight to search, so you can find and launch something without reaching for the taskbar. Silently does nothing if another running app already uses this combination.
settings.gridDensityDesc: How much room each game/app tile takes up in the library grid.
settings.autoRescanHint: Quietly repeat your last scan on a schedule, so newly installed games show up without you opening the wizard by hand. Runs locally in the background — no cloud, no network calls beyond the cover-art fetch it already does after any scan.
settings.smartFeaturesHint: Playnest tags genres, spots cracked/repacked game installs, scores your hardware for gaming performance, and suggests similar titles from your own library — all of it runs locally on your PC using rule-based matching. Nothing is sent to a cloud AI model, and none of it requires an internet connection or an API key. Playtime is estimated from how long the launched program stays open, which can under-count games that use a separate launcher process.
settings.privacyHint: Playnest only reads information already on this PC — your installed-programs list and, if you choose a deep scan, folders on the drives you selected. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The only network call Playnest ever makes is to SteamGridDB, to fetch cover art for the titles in your library. No telemetry, no accounts, no ads.

performanceMode.title: 🚀 Performance Mode
performanceMode.subtitle: Two real, independent Windows settings, in one place: Game Mode (a scheduling hint) and your power plan (an actual power/clock profile). Both are instant and fully reversible.
performanceMode.gameModeOnDesc: On — your foreground game gets scheduling priority and background updates pause.
performanceMode.planSaverDesc: Power Saver plan — lower power draw, quieter fans, best battery life on laptops.
performanceMode.planBalancedDesc: Windows' default — a mix of performance and efficiency for everyday use.
performanceMode.planPerformanceDesc: High Performance plan — maximum CPU clocks, no power-saving throttling.
performanceMode.whatsHappening1: writes the real AutoGameModeEnabled registry value Windows itself reads.
performanceMode.whatsHappening2: calls Windows' own powercfg tool — the same one Control Panel uses.
performanceMode.whatsHappening3: These are two different, independent Windows features — turning on Game Mode doesn't change your power plan, and vice versa.

streakTracker.title: 🔥 Gaming Streak
streakTracker.subtitle: Based on the days you've actually launched something from Playnest — no guessing.
streakTracker.noStreakYet: 💡 No active streak yet — launch a game or app from your library today to start one.
streakTracker.longestEver: 🏆 You're on your longest streak ever — keep it going!
streakTracker.howThisWorks1: Every time you launch a game or app through Playnest, today gets marked active.
streakTracker.howThisWorks2: A streak breaks the first day you don't launch anything at all.
streakTracker.howThisWorks3: This data lives only on your PC — nothing is uploaded anywhere.

systemMonitor.title: ⚡ System Monitor
systemMonitor.subtitle: Live CPU, memory, and temperature readings pulled straight from your hardware — no simulated numbers.
systemMonitor.tempUnavailable: Sensor not available on this PC
systemMonitor.about1: CPU and RAM come from the same sensors Task Manager reads.
systemMonitor.about2: Temperature reporting depends on your motherboard/CPU exposing a sensor Windows can see — many laptops don't, which is why it may show "N/A".
systemMonitor.about3: We don't fake an FPS number here: without hooking into a running game (which needs its own overlay SDK), any FPS figure would just be made up.
